item.title: Audio Guide: Registan Square
item.summary: An audio guide introduces the three madrasahs of Registan Square in Samarkand and how they were designed.
item.transcript_text: Welcome to Registan Square, the heart of old Samarkand. You're now standing in front of three great madrasahs, which were schools where students lived and studied for many years. Although they look like a single design, they were actually built over more than two centuries. The building on your left is the Ulugh Beg Madrasah, completed in the fifteenth century. Ulugh Beg was a ruler who was also a serious astronomer, and his school taught mathematics and astronomy alongside other subjects. Opposite it, on your right, is the Sher-Dor Madrasah, built about two hundred years later. Its architect deliberately mirrored the older building, so the two facades face each other almost like reflections. Now look above the Sher-Dor entrance, and you'll see two striped big cats chasing deer, with a human face in a rising sun behind them. Images of living creatures were rare on buildings like this, which is one reason the decoration is so famous. The third building, in the centre, is the Tilya-Kori Madrasah, which also served as the city's main mosque. Its name means covered with gold, and inside, the walls and dome are decorated with gold leaf. Take a few minutes to walk to the middle of the square and notice how balanced the whole space feels.
